analysis: Only CHANGELOG.md changed: a new 'Unreleased — DevNet' section at about line 72 describes (1) the installer writing a non-production coordinator URL into ~/.config/darkbloom/provider.toml, (2) a new coordinator/cmd/devnet-seed tool that fills an empty dev database with fake data and refuses a database whose users table has rows, and (3) the dev VM boot path setting EIGENINFERENCE_IPAPI_KEY. The patch contains no executable code, so it introduces no direct security regression. Items to examine if the corresponding source changes appear in other batches: the installer's rewrite of provider.toml, since a coordinator URL served by an untrusted or compromised installer host could redirect a provider to a rogue coordinator (TB-002, A-001, A-008). The installer already runs as a trusted-by-user download, so this is not clearly new. The devnet-seed tool's empty-users-table guard against accidentally seeding a production database (A-009, A-007). The IPAPI key being set on the dev VM boot path (secrets handling). Dev is out of scope per the threat model, so these are noted only as coverage items. The changelog does not change any App Attest, MDM, or attestation assumptions in TB-009 or TB-011. The actual installer, seed tool and deploy script diffs were not supplied in these units, so the safety of those behaviors is unreviewed.
